correctness.rationale: For every connected complete multipartite graph with >=2 nonempty parts, the positive process has exactly the constant terminal colourings and their single-coordinate flips at vertices whose parts contain at least two vertices, because every outside-part vertex burns at the second spread step and every remaining starting-part vertex at the third. Switching gives all balanced signings. The exact distance formula follows from nearest codewords and is invariant under global phase sign. Separate odd/even maximum-distance analysis and antipodal counting prove all worst-plurality and extremizer formulas, including clique and star boundaries. Bounded independent simulation over 37 types/1,354 signings supports but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected 2026 source defines the model, switching law and general covering-radius interpretation but does not evaluate the complete multipartite reachable code or the exact worst balanced-signature spectrum. Statement-level comparisons with signed Roman domination, majority C-colouring, unrelated covering codes and the distinct unbalanced one-negative-edge K_{a,b} historical claim do not imply the theorem. Dedicated published-finding corpus and web searches found no covering statement. This supports provisional originality, not guaranteed priority.

value.rationale: A recently introduced signed propagation invariant is solved for every balanced signature of the complete multipartite family, not merely one parameter value. The all-parameter reachable code, signature-by-signature plurality, sharp singleton/odd-order threshold and multiplicity of the worst signings resolve a motivated question suggested by the source paper’s covering-radius interpretation, with clear potential as a reference family for broader signed-burning codes.
